scenes.title: Cold open
narration: This is Apache, a dance from early 20th century Paris.
It is known as Paris's most dangerous dance.
on_screen: Hero video — MISSING
Title card: Apache · France · Early 20th century

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Apache started in Paris in 1908.
It was created by Maurice Mouvet and Max Dearly after watching street gangs.
The dance became popular at the Moulin Rouge and in early silent films.
The name comes from the press, who used it for local street gangs, borrowing it from North American Indigenous tribes.
on_screen: Map: France · Europe
Image 1 with attribution

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Apache began as a theatrical piece for cabarets and music halls.
It shows the drama of urban conflict and tense street relationships.
Today, it is a revived tradition.
on_screen: Footage: File:How to make a MOTIONER - 01.webm (https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/0/08/How_to_make_a_MOTIONER_-_01.webm?utm_source=commons.wikimedia.org&utm_campaign=imageinfo&utm_content=original)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The dance is performed as a couple.
It alternates between a rhythmic waltz and violent, acrobatic sequences.
The man leads the woman through throws, lifts, and mock strikes.
Watch for The Throw, The Lift.
on_screen: Hero video — MISSING
Captions name each signature move as it appears
Formation: Couple-based, utilizing stage space for dramatic movement
scenes.music: diegetic (the video's own sound), underscore under narration

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The music is usually a waltz.
The most famous piece is 'Valse des Rayons' by Jacques Offenbach.
Other versions include 'Valse Chaloupée' by Charles Dubourg and 'Valse Apache' by Fernand Le Borne.
Listen for orchestra and piano.
The rhythm is in 3/4 time.
The music moves between smooth, flowing melodies and sharp, rhythmic accents to match the physical action.

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: The dance is linked to the 'Apache' street gang style of early 1900s Paris.
It is set in places like seedy bars, cabarets, and Paris streets.

scenes.title: The people
narration: Max Dearly, Maurice Mouvet, Mistinguett, Leona, and later performers like Clara Bow and Buster Keaton.
Known as 'Valse Chaloupée' or 'Tough Dance' in various contexts.
Evolved from Parisian street culture and the 'cake-walk' variations performed by Mistinguett.

scenes.title: Family tree
narration: Apache is connected to the Waltz: it uses waltz music and steps.
It may also be influenced by the French Java dance.

music_brief.purpose: original soundtrack faithful to the tradition, with documented commercial reuse rights and no recurring royalties
music_brief.rights_rule: A composition brief does not clear an output. Record the provider/model/version, terms and date, input rights, output licence, restrictions and review before release.
music_brief.sound_description: A dramatic, orchestral waltz that transitions between melodic, flowing sections and sharp, rhythmic accents to underscore the physical combat.
music_brief.prompt: Original instrumental composition in the musical world of Apache (France). Meter 3/4. Instruments: Orchestra, Piano. Mood: Dramatic, Violent, Sensual, Tense. It should sound like this: A dramatic, orchestral waltz that transitions between melodic, flowing sections and sharp, rhythmic accents to underscore the physical combat. New melody, new arrangement: do not quote or imitate any specific recorded song; keep the idiom, the instruments, the pulse and the proportions.

tracks.use: chapters: dance it to the music

rules: Original composition only — no sampling, no melody of any existing recording, no lyrics from any song.
Traditional public-domain tunes may be used only when the profile names them and a public-domain source is on file; otherwise compose new material in the idiom.
Keep the proportions true: the meter, the tempo range and the instrument roles the sources describe.
Label every generated track with the tool, the date and this brief, so provenance is always clear.

visual_brief.setting_notes: Originally a theatrical performance piece for cabarets and music halls. It serves as a dramatic representation of urban conflict and the volatile dynamics of a street-level relationship.
